ideas.title: Lay the plank road on sand that really moves
ideas.nearest: A snowball that grows as it rolls, a take that misses
ideas.critique: This is round 1's plank road with its weak spot fixed. A GPU height field that really gets displaced, keeps its ruts and berms and slumps at its angle of repose is ground the island has never had, and the player and friends work in it instead of watching. The risk is the planks: if they only sit on the field instead of rocking as rigid bodies, it comes down to Bekker numbers drawn as a dent, and the 'fewest planks' puzzle depends on the dune really changing from day to day.

ideas.title: Yesterday's gale buried my road
ideas.nearest: Dandelion clocks, a take that misses
ideas.critique: Real saltation with lee shadows behind crests and fences, and dunes that creep, would be new physics and a time-lapse worth clipping. But it needs the sand field from the plank idea first, a wind shadow done as a simple lee mask is easily a rig, and the morning loop of digging out planks is chores unless fence placement really changes where the sand drops. It supports the road rather than being one of its steps.

ideas.title: Build the kiln, stone by stone
ideas.critique: This takes the round 1 kiln and lets the player build it, which beats judging a glow: stacking stones that can topple, with chimney height setting the draft, is a real choice. But stack effect, wall conduction and gap losses as a few lumped numbers is a rig, and the picture is fire and smoke again after the campfire and the hot wire. It is strongest where potcell.jl carries the firing into the cells.

ideas.title: Carve a wheel that cracks if you hurry
ideas.critique: Anisotropic drying that opens radial checks is a real piece of wood science, but the film it pitches is one object on a bench slowly failing, which is the recipe of the last post. Hoop stress in one disc with one wood's numbers written in is a rig, and the dune roll test only matters once the sand really gives.
